json.title: JSON Tool Suite
json.desc: JSON toolkit with formatting, comparison, Java Bean conversion, XML conversion, compression, and more. Supports node folding, diff highlighting, and syntax validation.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.about1: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the most popular lightweight data exchange format today, widely used in APIs, configuration files, log data, and more.
intro.about2: This tool is an all-in-one online JSON processor combining formatting, comparing, and conversion, helping developers quickly read, analyze, and convert JSON data.
intro.about3: All processing is done locally in your browser — no data is uploaded to any server, so it is safe for sensitive data.
intro.module1: Format: Smart fault-tolerant parsing, one-click beautify, with collapse/expand and key-value search.
intro.module2: Compare: Dual-pane comparison of two JSON documents with highlighted differences and synchronized operations.
intro.module3: To Java Bean: Auto-generate Java entity class code from JSON structure, with reverse conversion supported.
intro.module4: To XML: Two-way conversion between JSON and XML, preserving the complete hierarchy.
intro.feature1: Smart Tolerance: Auto-removes BOM and comments, converts single quotes to double quotes, supports Python-style True/False/None, and tolerates trailing commas.
intro.feature2: Fuzzy Key/Value Search: Fuzzy matching on keys and values, showing line numbers and full paths, with click-to-locate navigation.
intro.feature3: Escape State Awareness: Clicking Format while escaped auto-unescapes first; unescaping restores the previous display state.
intro.feature4: Modern Editor: Built on CodeMirror 6 with syntax highlighting, line numbers, word wrap, fullscreen, and dark mode.

format.title: 1. Formatting Features
format.item1: Format: Converts compressed JSON strings into readable formats with indentation, syntax highlighting, and line numbers. Built-in smart tolerance: auto-removes BOM and comments, converts single quotes to double quotes, supports Python-style True/False/None, and tolerates trailing commas.
format.item2: Minify: Compresses formatted JSON into a single line (comments are automatically removed), suitable for transmission and storage; escaped content can also be minified directly.
format.item3: Escape/Unescape: Escapes/unescapes special characters in JSON (such as quotes and backslashes). Clicking "Format" while in escaped state auto-unescapes first; unescaping restores the previous display state (formatted or minified).
format.item4: Collapse/Expand: For complex nested JSON structures, collapse all nodes with one click (objects show property counts, arrays show item counts); click again to expand. Formatting is required first — otherwise a "Please format first" prompt appears.
format.item5: Search: Click the "Search" button to open the search panel and fuzzy-match keys and values (case-insensitive). Results show match type, line number, and full path (e.g. address.city); click a result to scroll to and select it. Formatting is not required as long as the content is parseable JSON.
format.item6: New Line: Automatically breaks down a compressed JSON string into multiple lines according to structure, making it easier to view long string content.
format.item7: Auxiliary Operations: Supports Example (load sample data), Paste, Copy, Clear, word wrap, and editor maximizing; a duplicate button group at the page bottom makes long-document operations easier.

compare.title: 2. Comparison Features
compare.item1: Diff Highlighting: Input two JSON segments simultaneously, and the system will compare line by line and highlight all differences, supporting three difference types: added, deleted, and modified.
compare.item2: Sync Operations: Supports synchronized formatting, compression, escaping, and clearing of both editor contents for improved comparison efficiency.
compare.item3: Node Marking: For arrays and objects, marks exactly which element or property has changed.

javabean.title: 3. JSON to Java Bean
javabean.item1: Auto Conversion: Automatically generates corresponding Java entity class code based on JSON structure, including field names, types, and getter/setter methods.
javabean.item2: Type Inference: Automatically identifies JSON data types (strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects, etc.) and maps them to Java types.
javabean.item3: Value Auto-fill: During conversion, preserves actual values from JSON as examples for easier understanding and testing.
javabean.item4: Java Bean to JSON: Supports reverse conversion, converting Java Bean code back to JSON format.

xml.title: 4. JSON & XML Conversion
xml.item1: JSON to XML: Converts JSON data structures to standard XML format, supporting correct conversion of nested structures and arrays.
xml.item2: XML to JSON: Converts XML documents to JSON format, preserving element names, attributes, and text content.
xml.item3: Format Optimization: Converted XML is automatically formatted for easier reading and editing.

security.title: 1. Data Security
security.item1: All processing is done locally in the browser; data is never uploaded to servers or recorded/stored.
security.item2: It is recommended not to process JSON data containing sensitive information on public devices.
security.item3: After processing, it is recommended to clear the editor content to avoid sensitive information residue.

format.title: 2. Format Requirements
format.item1: Input JSON data should comply with standard JSON syntax; built-in smart tolerance automatically handles BOM headers, comments, single quotes, and trailing commas.
format.item2: Strings in JSON should be wrapped in double quotes; single quotes are automatically converted to double quotes.
format.item3: Trailing commas after the last property of an object or the last element of an array are tolerated automatically, but standard syntax is recommended for compatibility.
format.item4: Supported JSON value types include: strings, numbers, booleans, null, arrays, objects.

usage.title: 3. Feature Usage
usage.item1: Collapse/Expand is only available after formatting; clicking "Collapse" before formatting shows a "Please format first" prompt.
usage.item2: Search does not require formatting, but the input must be parseable valid JSON; for minified or escaped content, restore it first before searching.
usage.item3: Formatting and minifying automatically remove JSONC comments (// and /* */); back up the original content if you need to keep the comments.
usage.item4: Comparison ignores whitespace and object field order differences, but array element order affects the comparison result.

performance.title: 4. Performance Tips
performance.item1: Processing very large JSON data (over 10MB) may cause browser lag or slow response.
performance.item2: For particularly complex nested structures, collapse and expand operations may have delayed.
performance.item3: It is recommended to process large JSON files in segments to avoid loading too much data at once.

compatibility.title: 5. Browser Compatibility
compatibility.item1: It is recommended to use modern browsers (Chrome 80+, Firefox 75+, Edge 80+, Safari 13+) for the best experience.
compatibility.item2: Older browsers may not support some advanced features, such as syntax highlighting and node folding.
compatibility.item3: Mobile browser support is limited; it is recommended to use on desktop for a better editing experience.

encoding.title: 6. Encoding Issues
encoding.item1: Ensure input data uses UTF-8 encoding to avoid garbled characters in Chinese and other non-ASCII characters.
encoding.item2: When copying JSON data from other files, check for invisible characters or BOM headers.
encoding.item3: The escape function automatically handles Chinese and special characters to ensure converted JSON can be parsed correctly.

faq.title: 7. Common Issues
faq.item1: Format Error: Please check if JSON syntax is correct, especially if brackets match and commas are positioned correctly.
faq.item2: Inaccurate Comparison: Ensure the two JSON segments have similar structure; it is recommended to format them separately before comparing.
faq.item3: Unexpected Conversion Results: Complex nested structures may require manual adjustment; it is recommended to check if the generated code meets business requirements.

mermaid.title: Mermaid Online UML Diagram Tool
mermaid.desc: Mermaid online UML diagram tool supporting flowcharts, sequence diagrams, state diagrams, class diagrams, ER diagrams, pie charts, Gantt charts, user journey maps, and more. Features theme switching, fullscreen, zoom, and drag interactions.

intro.title: About This Tool
intro.problem1: Draw flowcharts, sequence diagrams, and more using Mermaid syntax.
intro.problem2: Simplify tedious manual operations, improving efficiency and accuracy.
intro.problem3: No need to install professional software — use it online anytime, anywhere.
intro.format1: Mermaid: Full processing support for this format.
intro.core1: Online Processing: All operations are completed in the browser — no downloads or installation needed.
intro.core2: Real-time Preview: Results are displayed instantly for easy adjustment and confirmation.
intro.core3: One-click Export: Quickly export processed files or copy results.
intro.core4: Data Security: All data is processed locally only, never uploaded to servers.

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.chart1: Flowchart: Display process steps and decision paths, supporting various shapes, arrow styles, and layout directions (top-down, left-to-right, etc.).
instructions.chart2: Sequence Diagram: Show the order of interactions between objects, commonly used for describing system call flows and API request sequences.
instructions.chart3: State Diagram: Describe an object's state changes and transition conditions during its lifecycle, ideal for displaying state machine logic.
instructions.chart4: Class Diagram: Show relationships between classes (inheritance, association, dependency, etc.), the core diagram of object-oriented design.
instructions.chart5: ER Diagram: Describe database table structures and relationships between tables, supporting one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relationship types.
instructions.chart6: Pie Chart: Display proportional distribution of data, suitable for showing the share of categorized data.
instructions.chart7: Gantt Chart: Display project progress and timelines, supporting task grouping, dependencies, and milestone markers.
instructions.chart8: User Journey Map: Describe user experience and emotional changes during product usage, helping optimize user experience.
instructions.basic1: Select Chart Type: Click the chart type buttons above, and the system will automatically populate the editor with sample code.
instructions.basic2: Enter Mermaid Code: Type or modify Mermaid syntax code in the left editor; the right preview area will update the chart in real time.
instructions.basic3: Use E-commerce Examples: Click buttons under "E-commerce Examples" to view complex diagram examples from real e-commerce scenarios, including order flows, API requests, etc.
instructions.basic4: Custom Code: Select the "Custom" button to clear the editor and enter your own Mermaid code.
instructions.interaction1: Theme Switching: Click the color dots above the preview area to switch chart themes (default, white, gray, blue, purple, dark, and 10 themes total).
instructions.interaction2: Fullscreen Preview: Click the "Fullscreen" button to display the chart in fullscreen mode for viewing large charts.
instructions.interaction3: Scroll Zoom: Use the mouse scroll wheel in the preview area to zoom in or out.
instructions.interaction4: Drag to Pan: Hold the left mouse button and drag to pan the chart and view portions beyond the viewport.
instructions.interaction5: Download Chart: Click the "Download" button to export the chart as a PNG or SVG image.
instructions.interaction6: Copy Code: Click the "Copy" button to quickly copy the Mermaid code in the current editor.
instructions.syntax1: Flowchart Direction: Use flowchart LR (left to right), flowchart TD (top to down) to specify layout direction.
instructions.syntax2: Node Definitions: A[Rectangle], B(Rounded Rectangle), C{Diamond Decision}, D>Parallelogram], E((Circle)) and more shapes.
instructions.syntax3: Connection Lines: --> solid, -.-> dashed, ==> thick; add labels with -->|label|.
instructions.syntax4: Subgraphs: Use subgraph to define subgraphs and group related nodes.
instructions.syntax5: Comments: Use %% comment to add single-line comments.

notes.title: Notes
notes.syntax1: Mermaid syntax is case-sensitive; keywords (such as flowchart, sequenceDiagram) must use the correct case.
notes.syntax2: Nodes must be connected with lines, otherwise the chart may not render correctly.
notes.syntax3: Special characters (such as Chinese, spaces, special symbols) need to be wrapped in quotes or escaped.
notes.syntax4: Ensure the syntax structure is complete and all brackets and quotes are closed.
notes.performance1: Overly complex charts (more than 50 nodes or multiple nesting levels) may cause rendering delays.
notes.performance2: It is recommended to split large charts into multiple subgraphs to improve readability and rendering performance.
notes.performance3: Use browser zoom to view chart details instead of over-zooming.
notes.compatibility1: Modern browsers (Chrome 80+, Firefox 75+, Edge 80+, Safari 13+) are recommended for the best rendering experience.
notes.compatibility2: Older browsers may not support some chart types or interactive features.
notes.compatibility3: Mobile browser support is limited; desktop use is recommended for a better editing experience.
notes.export1: PNG format is suitable for document insertion and sharing with higher image quality.
notes.export2: SVG format is vector-based, suitable for scenarios requiring lossless scaling with smaller file sizes.
notes.export3: It is recommended to save both the Mermaid source code and exported images for future modification and maintenance.
notes.security1: All processing is done locally in the browser; data is never uploaded to servers.
notes.security2: Avoid processing charts with sensitive information on public devices.
notes.security3: Code in the editor is automatically cleared after closing the browser.
notes.faq1: Chart won't render: Check if the Mermaid syntax is correct and all brackets and quotes are closed.
notes.faq2: Layout is messy: Try adjusting the flowchart direction (LR/TD) or use subgraphs for grouping.
notes.faq3: Theme switching not working: Refresh the page and try again, or check if browser cache has expired.
notes.faq4: Download failed: Ensure the chart is rendered correctly and check if the browser allows pop-up download windows.

questions.q1: Why is data processed locally? How does it work?
questions.a1: Helpoke uses modern browser Web APIs (like FileReader, Canvas, WebAssembly) to implement file processing on the client side. When you upload a file, it only exists in the browser's memory. JavaScript code directly reads and processes the data, generating result files for you to download. The entire process never leaves your device - the server only provides webpage code and doesn't participate in data processing.
questions.a2: Our tools support all modern browsers, including the latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. For the best experience, we recommend using Chrome or Firefox. Some tools use newer web technologies (like WebCodecs, WebAssembly), so we recommend keeping your browser up to date.
questions.q3: What if the browser crashes when processing large files?
questions.a3: Since all processing happens in browser memory, handling very large files (like HD videos, many images) may use significant memory. Suggestions: 1) Close other memory-intensive tabs and programs; 2) Process files in batches; 3) Use a 64-bit browser; 4) Ensure sufficient available memory. If it still crashes, try using desktop tools.
questions.a4: Video tools are based on FFmpeg (running in browser via WebAssembly), supporting mainstream formats including: MP4, WebM, MOV, AVI, MKV, GIF, etc. Output formats support MP4, WebM, GIF. Due to browser security restrictions, some encrypted or specially encoded videos may not be processable.
questions.q5: Why can't some tools work offline?
questions.a5: Most tools can work offline after first load, but these situations require internet: 1) First visit to a tool needs to load webpage code; 2) Some tools depend on external libraries (like FFmpeg, Mermaid), need download on first use; 3) CDN-accelerated resources need network. Recommend visiting needed tools when network is good, then they'll work offline.
questions.q6: How to report issues or suggest features?
questions.a6: We welcome all feedback and suggestions! You can contact us through: 1) Leave a message in the comments section at the bottom of the page; 2) Send email to contact@helpoke.com; 3) Visit the About Us page for more contact methods. We read every piece of feedback and continuously improve our tools.
